$comment: HZ-128: the contract for domain/steps.json. Validated by domain/validate.mjs — a dependency-free subset validator (no ajv; guardrail 3 forbids a new dependency), so only these keywords are honoured: type, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, enum, minimum, maximum, minLength, minItems, uniqueItems, allOf, if/then. Cross-field rules a Draft-07 subset cannot express (phase < phases.length, unique labels) are asserted at LOAD time by the bindings themselves instead — see assertLifecycleShape() in domain/js/lifecycle.js and _validate_source() in domain/py/steps.py, which domain/fixtures/lifecycle-cases.json drives from both sides so the two cannot drift.
title: Horizon lifecycle step table

lanes.$comment: HZ-435: an opt-in overlay on one item kind's rows, selected only by the lane's issue label. `check` rows are confirmed by a server-side check instead of an agent; `skip` rows never run. Which rows a lane may skip (never a gate it does not empty, never a workspace-mutating step, never the kind's last row) is asserted at load time by assertLifecycleShape() and _validate_source().

kindEntry.$comment: HZ-382: label and description are the kind's display copy (the New item radio cards, the Task badge). Optional, so a minimal table still validates; non-empty when present.

key.$comment: HZ-709: the step's permanent name, `<itemKind>.<slug>`. Routes, the item snapshot, farm messages, polls and defaults name a step by it, never by its position. Once shipped a key is never renamed or reused (server/test/domain-step-keys.test.mjs freezes the list). The subset has no `pattern`, so the shape ^[a-z]+\.[a-z0-9-]+$, uniqueness and the kind prefix are asserted at load time by assertLifecycleShape() and _validate_source().

sendBackTo.$comment: HZ-709: a gate's default send-back target, by key — an earlier agent step of the same item kind. Without it a send-back walks back to the nearest earlier agent step.

runsIn.$comment: HZ-446: 'server' is Horizon's own code in the server process — no LLM, no farm, no agent (server/src/orchestrator.js runServerStep).

short.$comment: HZ-477: a short farm step — it may take the farm's express slot (farm/farmd.py FARM_EXPRESS_SLOTS) when every general agent slot is busy.

spawnsOn.$comment: HZ-379: the reply field that, when the step's run returns it, files one item of spawnKind and makes this item wait for it (server/src/spawn.js).

awaitsSpawnedCode.$comment: HZ-379: this step starts only once every closed spawned dependency's merge is live, and runs on that checkout.

humanOnly.$comment: HZ-384: this gate passes only for a human with the gate PIN — never Autopilot, WhatsApp or a token, whatever the project's Autopilot mode (server/src/store.js approveGate).

codeRun.$comment: HO-837: a farm step that runs fixed farm code, not a model (farm/preflight.py for task.preflight). It has no persona, no provider, no input budget and no turn budget, so it declares no maxTurns; its timeoutS is the code's own cap, at most 90 s.

acceptWithExceptions.$comment: HO-844: this Task gate also offers Accept with exceptions when the stored Verify outcome is done_proof_incomplete: a human with the gate PIN closes it naming each open metric line and a reason (server/src/gateExceptions.js). Only a Task gate may set it; assertLifecycleShape() checks the item kind.

allOf.$comment: HZ-384: only a gate can be human-only.
HO-844: only a gate can accept with exceptions.
HZ-379: a step that spawns says what kind it files.
HZ-477: only a farm-lane step can take the express slot.
An agent-kind step always names its lane; it never carries a gate. The agent itself is required separately below, because a runsIn 'none' step has no runner yet.
A step on a real lane always names its agent; only a runsIn 'none' or 'server' step may omit it.
HZ-378: a job-lane step runs shell commands, not an agent — it carries no agent budget.
HZ-446: a server-lane step is Horizon's own code — it names no agent and carries no agent budget or workspace.
A gate is human-only: no agent, no lane, no farm budget.
HO-837: a code-run step is a farm step with no model: no turn budget, never a provider override, never a workspace change, and a cap of at most 90 s.

Farm-lane steps carry the full budget/provider contract step_agent.py reads; the PM lane uses farm/pm_steps.py's own budget mechanism and must not declare these, except providerOverrideEligible (HZ-370: a PM step may take the owner's provider choice). HO-837: a code-run step carries no maxTurns (the rule above).
